title: LinearPFN: Amortized Variable Selection for Linear Models with Interactions
summary: Spike-and-slab regression is a standard Bayesian formulation of variable selection: it returns a posterior distribution over which candidate effects are active rather than a single selected subset, so that every candidate effect carries an inclusion probability. Its cost grows exponentially with the number of candidate effects, so the posterior can be enumerated exactly only when the number of predictors is small. Beyond that reach, the posterior has to be approximated, typically by Markov chain Monte Carlo over the model space, which requires a fresh run for every dataset and, within a fixed budget of steps, may fail to converge. We present LinearPFN, a prior-data fitted transformer network that amortizes spike-and-slab inference for linear models with main effects and pairwise interactions. The network is pretrained once on synthetic datasets, drawn from an explicitly specified prior, and a single forward pass over a new dataset returns posterior inclusion probabilities, posterior-mean coefficients and posterior predictive distributions with no per-dataset fitting. The prior is conjugate by design, so that the posterior for each fixed set of active effects has a closed form, and wherever the exact posterior is still computable by enumeration we verify the network's outputs against it. On real predictor matrices from published social-science datasets, with outcomes drawn from the prior so that the true active set is known, LinearPFN attains a higher per-dataset selection AUC and a higher F1 under the median probability model rule than five classical baselines. The lead holds when the coefficients, the interactions or the noise depart from the prior. Code: https://github.com/schiekiera/LinearPFN. Trained model: https://huggingface.co/schiekiera/LinearPFN.
core_methodology: LinearPFN is a transformer-based network that performs amortized spike-and-slab inference for linear models with main effects and interactions. It leverages pretraining on synthetic datasets generated from a specified prior, enabling efficient computation of posterior inclusion probabilities and other posterior quantities without per-dataset fitting
data_sources: Applicable to any structured financial datasets (e.g., factor returns, macroeconomic indicators, asset characteristics) where variable selection for linear models with interactions is needed.
alpha_potential: High potential for identifying relevant predictive factors and interaction effects in multi-factor models, leading to improved portfolio construction and risk management strategies. Particularly valuable for: 1) Interaction effect discovery in quantitative equity models 2) Dimensionality reduction in high-dimensional predictive models 3) Adaptive factor model selection
title_cn: 线性PFN：线性模型交互效应的摊销变量选择方法
summary_cn: LinearPFN通过预训练的转换器网络实现线性模型中主效应和交互效应的变量选择，可直接应用于量化金融中的多因子建模。该方法高效计算后验包含概率和预测分布，对发现阿尔法因子和因子间的交互效应具有重要价值，特别适合高维金融数据的建模与风险控制。

title: Latent Continuum of Regimes in Limit Order Book Dynamics
summary: Market-regime models typically assume a finite set of discrete latent states. We examine whether high frequency limit-order-book dynamics exhibit distinct regime separation or apparent regimes result from discretising an underlying continuum, analysing deep limit-order book data for EURO STOXX 50 index futures across 987 clean trading days from 2022 to 2025 using 30, 45 and 60-second aggregation windows. Market states are represented by symmetric positive definite covariance matrices and analysed under Log-Euclidean and affine-invariant geometries; the resulting state cloud has an effective dimension of approximately 1.4. A causal anomaly layer filters statistical, calendar and rollover contamination, while label-free economic validation evaluates market-state separation independently of volatility-based proxy labels. A 17-method zoo spanning conventional and Riemannian representations, reinforced by full-cloud geometric certificates, consistently favours a continuum over a discrete regime structure. A dominant latent coordinate captures between 83.66% and 85.27% of variation in the covariance-state geometry and tracks VSTOXX without regime labels, remaining stable across years although its average level shifts with market conditions, indicating that conventional regimes are coarse quantisations. A divisive hierarchy spanning macro, macro-subregime, micro and micro-subregime tiers is evaluated using expanding-year walk-forward tests, with out-of-sample performance strongest at the macro tier while finer tiers fail to generalise; continuous fine-scale information nonetheless remains predictive, and its discretisation causes the performance loss. Forecasting performance peaks near ten minutes, reaching a maximum pooled R2_OOS of 0.7483. Overall, the latent stress coordinate defines a stable, low-dimensional geometric continuum that captures market stress and its predictive dynamics.
core_methodology: Analysis of limit-order-book dynamics using Riemannian geometry and covariance matrices to identify a latent continuum of market states rather than discrete regimes. The approach includes causal anomaly filtering and label-free economic validation.
data_sources: Deep limit-order book data for EURO STOXX 50 index futures across 987 clean trading days from 2022 to 2025, analyzed with 30, 45, and 60-second aggregation windows.
alpha_potential: The identification of a stable, low-dimensional geometric continuum capturing market stress and predictive dynamics can provide a robust signal for high-frequency trading strategies. The method avoids the pitfalls of discrete regime models and offers a more nuanced understanding of market microstructure.
title_cn: 限价订单簿动态中的潜在连续状态
summary_cn: 该研究通过黎曼几何和协方差矩阵分析限价订单簿动态，揭示了市场状态潜在的连续统一体而非离散状态。这一发现可用于高频交易策略，提供稳健的市场压力信号，避免离散状态模型的局限性。

title: Causal Lag Structure Discovery in Confounded Time Series via Orthogonalized Adaptive Estimation
summary: Finding which variables cause which others in multivariate time series, and at what lags, is central to science and policy, yet existing methods force a choice between flexible confounder adjustment, data-driven lag selection, and inference that controls the false discovery rate (FDR). ORACLE-VARX does all three in one pipeline. First, double/debiased machine learning (DML) removes nonlinear confounder effects from the outcomes and the lagged series. Second, adaptive causal lag estimation (ACLE) picks the lag order at each time step by sequential significance tests, tracking regime changes. Third, entry-wise $z$-tests with Benjamini--Hochberg correction select directed edges at a target FDR. We prove that in each rolling window, the debiased coefficients are asymptotically normal around a window-averaged target, so their $z$-tests are asymptotically valid. On a synthetic benchmark with time-varying structure and nonlinear confounding, ORACLE-VARX (LightGBM) tracks the true lag order best (RMSE $0.96$ vs $1.1$--$1.5$), has edge FDR $0.047$, close to PCMCI ($0.045$) and below VAR ($0.129$) and VAR-LiNGAM ($0.187$), and forecasts better than all three. On nine U.S. sector ETFs with macroeconomic confounders, it yields interpretable causal graphs whose lag order rises in high-volatility regimes.
core_methodology: ORACLE-VARX combines double/debiased machine learning (DML) for nonlinear confounder adjustment, adaptive causal lag estimation (ACLE) for dynamic lag selection, and entry-wise z-tests with Benjamini-Hochberg correction for directed edge selection at a target false discovery rate (FDR). The method is designed to handle time-varying structures and nonlinear confounding in multivariate time series.
data_sources: Synthetic benchmark data with time-varying structure and nonlinear confounding, and real-world data from nine U.S. sector ETFs with macroeconomic confounders.
alpha_potential: The methodology can identify causal relationships and lag structures in financial time series, which is valuable for predicting price movements, understanding market dynamics, and constructing trading strategies. The ability to adapt to regime changes and handle confounders makes it particularly useful in volatile markets.
title_cn: 基于正交化自适应估计的混杂时间序列因果滞后结构发现
summary_cn: ORACLE-VARX通过结合去偏机器学习和自适应因果滞后估计，有效识别多变量时间序列中的因果关系和滞后结构，适用于金融市场中的价格预测和交易策略构建。该方法在高波动市场中表现优异，能够适应结构变化并处理非线性混杂因素。

title: MatrixFormer: A Foundation Model for Matrix Completion
summary: Matrix completion underlies problems from tabular imputation to causal inference, yet existing tabular foundation models treat it as entry-by-entry prediction, repeating context for every target and discarding the matrix's two-dimensional structure. We introduce MatrixFormer, a pre-trained matrix-native transformer that predicts a full distribution for every missing entry in a single forward pass. MatrixFormer is trained entirely on synthetic low-rank and latent-factor matrices under diverse missingness patterns. Applied zero-shot and with the same model weights, MatrixFormer achieves competitive performance on causal inference panel-data tasks, language-model benchmark-score completion, tabular imputation, and recommendation systems matrix completion. These results position MatrixFormer as a general-purpose foundation model for matrix completion.
core_methodology: MatrixFormer is a pre-trained transformer model specifically designed for matrix completion tasks. It predicts full distributions for missing entries in a single forward pass, maintaining the matrix's two-dimensional structure unlike traditional entry-by-entry prediction methods. The model is trained on synthetic low-rank and latent-factor matrices under diverse missingness patterns.
data_sources: Trained on synthetic low-rank and latent-factor matrices, but applicable to real-world tabular data, panel data (common in financial time series), and recommendation systems (analogous to portfolio optimization problems).
alpha_potential: Could enhance factor modeling by better handling missing fundamental data, improve portfolio optimization with sparse return matrices, and potentially uncover latent relationships in market microstructure data. The zero-shot capability allows application without retraining on financial data.
title_cn: MatrixFormer：矩阵补全的基础模型
summary_cn: MatrixFormer是一种针对矩阵补全任务的预训练变换器模型，能单次预测所有缺失值的完整分布。该技术在量化金融中潜在应用包括：处理基本面数据缺失的因子建模、优化稀疏收益矩阵的资产配置，以及发现市场微观结构中的隐藏关系。其零样本学习特性特别适合金融场景中快速部署的需求。

title: Inverse Cross-spectral Neural Networks for Multivariate Time Series
summary: CoVariance Neural Networks and their extensions have emerged as effective tools for processing multivariate data, deriving graph shift operators directly from second-order statistics. These architectures, however, are designed for independent and identically distributed observations and do not fully capture the joint structure of temporal and cross-variable dependencies in multivariate time series. In this work, we introduce Inverse Cross-Spectral Neural Networks (iCSNNs), a class of graph neural networks for stationary multivariate time series whose shift operators are the inverse cross-spectral density (iCSD) matrices. These operators encode frequency-specific conditional relationships among variables, exploiting the decomposition provided by the spectral representation theorem. Leveraging spectral smoothness, frequencies are grouped into bands sharing a single iCSD operator, yielding a compact parametrisation that retains the frequency-dependent structure of the process. We further propose a joint learning procedure to estimate both the Fourier-domain dependence structure and the iCSNN parameters, adapting the iCSD operators to the downstream task. When tested on synthetic data, iCSNN outperforms baselines from different methodological families.
core_methodology: The paper introduces Inverse Cross-Spectral Neural Networks (iCSNNs), a class of graph neural networks for stationary multivariate time series. These networks utilize inverse cross-spectral density matrices as shift operators to encode frequency-specific conditional relationships among variables, leveraging the spectral representation theorem for decomposition.
data_sources: The abstract mentions synthetic data for testing, but the methodology is designed for stationary multivariate time series, which could include financial time series data such as asset prices, trading volumes, or macroeconomic indicators.
alpha_potential: The methodology's focus on capturing frequency-specific conditional relationships in multivariate time series could help in identifying latent dependencies and lead-lag relationships between financial instruments, potentially useful for factor investing and portfolio optimization strategies.
title_cn: 逆向交叉频谱神经网络在多变量时间序列中的应用
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种用于平稳多变量时间序列的逆向交叉频谱神经网络（iCSNN），通过逆交叉频谱密度矩阵捕捉变量间频率特定的条件关系，有望应用于金融时间序列分析和投资策略优化，提升对复杂市场依赖结构的建模能力。

title: Normality Constraint Learning: Adapting Foundation Models for Time Series Anomaly Detection
summary: Time Series Foundation Models (TSFMs) achieve strong generalization by learning to reconstruct or forecast broad temporal patterns from large-scale time series during pre-training. Yet this strength can become a weakness for anomaly detection: TSFMs may model rare anomalous patterns as effectively as normal ones, allowing anomalies to be accurately reconstructed or forecasted and thus diminishing their reconstruction/forecasting error-based anomaly scores. This paper proposes $\underline{\textbf{N}}$$\textbf{ormality}$ $\underline{\textbf{C}}$$\textbf{onstraint}$ $\underline{\textbf{L}}$$\textbf{earning}$ ($\textbf{NCL}$), a lightweight plug-and-play framework that adapts pre-trained TSFMs for accurate anomaly detection without modifying their pre-trained parameters. Our key insight is to constrain the broad pattern space of TSFMs to the normal structure of a target time series, preventing their broad modeling capability from obscuring abnormal deviations. Specifically, NCL constructs a compact normality subspace from a few normal patch features and adaptively steers each patch feature toward normality within this subspace, guided by contrastive constraints that form compact and discriminative normality manifolds. The calibrated features are aggregated to reinforce normal components and fused with the original TSFM output, amplifying the discrepancy between normal and abnormal observations for the reconstruction/forecasting error-based anomaly scoring. Extensive experiments across diverse TSFM families and benchmarks show that NCL consistently improves anomaly detection performance, providing a generalizable framework for adapting TSFMs to anomaly detection.
core_methodology: Normality Constraint Learning (NCL) adapts pre-trained Time Series Foundation Models (TSFMs) for anomaly detection by constructing a normality subspace from normal patch features and steering patch features toward normality using contrastive constraints. This amplifies discrepancies between normal and abnormal observations for better anomaly scoring.
data_sources: Time series data from diverse benchmarks, applicable to financial time series like stock prices, forex data, or market indicators.
alpha_potential: Enhances anomaly detection in financial time series, potentially identifying unusual market movements, regime shifts, or microstructural anomalies that could be exploited for trading signals or risk management.
title_cn: 正态约束学习：为时间序列异常检测调整基础模型
summary_cn: 本文提出NCL框架，通过在预训练时间序列基础模型上施加正态约束，提升异常检测性能。该方法的创新点在于构建紧凑的正态子空间并引导特征向正态方向调整，放大了正常与异常观测的差异，可直接应用于金融时间序列的异常模式识别和交易信号生成。

title: MercerFlow: Flow Matching in a Kernel-Induced Latent Space for Probabilistic Forecasting
summary: Recent work has shown that probabilistic flow matching for time series forecasting benefits from a data-matched prior. The resulting prior introduces local correlations, which a sequential architecture usually absorbs: a recurrent neural network (RNN), a structured state-space model (S4), or a Transformer. However, such a backbone costs GPU memory and time per epoch. A cheaper alternative is MLP-based latent-space flow matching: embed the time series via an invertible map to a single latent vector and learn the flow there, so a tabular MLP can treat the series as a set of features. The relationship between the prior and the choice of linear latent map is understudied in conditional flow matching (CFM) forecasting, yet we found it strongly affects performance. Fixed transforms such as Fourier or discrete cosine (DCT) are only well-conditioned for Ornstein--Uhlenbeck priors, while a principal-component (PCA) map fit to the data is a strong but training-set-dependent reference sensitive to train--test shift. Instead, we propose to use the Mercer eigenbasis of the prior kernel: it diagonalises the centred covariance exactly, decouples from training data, and adapts to non-stationary and periodic priors. On five GluonTS benchmarks (ETTh1, ETTh2, Weather, Electricity, Traffic) under a shared protocol with TSFlow, the resulting MLP matches or beats it on CRPS at about $4.7\times$ less training memory and $3.5\times$--$4.4\times$ less time per epoch.
core_methodology: The paper proposes MercerFlow, a method for probabilistic forecasting using flow matching in a kernel-induced latent space. It leverages the Mercer eigenbasis of the prior kernel to diagonalize the covariance, which decouples from training data and adapts to non-stationary and periodic priors. This approach reduces computational costs (memory and time) while maintaining or improving performance compared to traditional methods like RNNs and Transformers.
data_sources: The evaluation is conducted on five GluonTS benchmarks: ETTh1, ETTh2, Weather, Electricity, and Traffic. These datasets represent time series data, which are analogous to financial time series like stock prices, trading volumes, and macroeconomic indicators.
alpha_potential: The method's ability to handle non-stationary and periodic priors can be valuable for forecasting financial time series, where market conditions often change. The reduced computational cost allows for faster iteration and deployment in high-frequency trading or portfolio optimization scenarios. The probabilistic nature of the forecasts can also be useful for risk management and uncertainty quantification in trading strategies.
title_cn: MercerFlow：基于核诱导隐空间的概率预测流匹配方法
summary_cn: 该论文提出MercerFlow，一种在核诱导隐空间中进行流匹配的概率预测方法。通过利用核的Mercer特征基，该方法能够解耦训练数据并适应非平稳和周期性先验，显著降低计算成本。在金融时间序列预测中，该方法可用于股票价格、交易量等预测，为高频交易和投资组合优化提供高效支持。

title: Joint Precision Neural Networks: Task-Aware Dependency and Predictive Learning
summary: Exploiting meaningful latent structures from data to solve downstream tasks is a fundamental challenge in signal processing and machine learning. While Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and coVariance Neural Networks (VNNs) successfully leverage the covariance matrix to process data, they inherently capture both direct and indirect correlations. The precision matrix (inverse covariance) overcomes this by explicitly encoding conditional independencies, making it largely studied in graphical lasso and graph topology identification. However, finite-sample precision estimates are notoriously unstable, and regularized estimators remain task-agnostic. In this work, our principal contribution is tackling the challenging problem of task-aware graph inference. We propose Precision Neural Networks-Joint (PNN-Joint), a framework that jointly estimates a sparse, statistically grounded precision matrix alongside graph neural network weights via an alternating optimization scheme. As a foundational framework to support this, we introduce Precision Neural Networks (PNNs), a broader class of graph convolutional networks operating on precision estimators, and establish their spectral connections to PCA and VNNs alongside their stability to finite-sample errors. Extensive empirical evaluations on synthetic data, as well as real-world neuroimaging and motion sensor datasets, demonstrate that PNN-Joint yields highly interpretable task-aware graphs, exhibits remarkable robustness in low-data regimes, and consistently achieves the best or second-best performance among competitors on real-world tasks.
core_methodology: The paper introduces Precision Neural Networks-Joint (PNN-Joint), a framework that jointly estimates a sparse precision matrix (inverse covariance) alongside graph neural network weights using an alternating optimization scheme. This approach leverages the precision matrix to explicitly encode conditional independencies, which can be beneficial for identifying meaningful latent structures in financial data.
data_sources: The paper evaluates the methodology on synthetic data, neuroimaging, and motion sensor datasets, but the framework could be adapted to financial time-series data, asset returns, or other market-related datasets.
alpha_potential: The method's ability to capture conditional independencies and produce interpretable task-aware graphs could be valuable for portfolio optimization, risk management, and identifying hidden dependencies in financial markets. The robustness in low-data regimes is particularly appealing for niche markets or alternative datasets with limited historical data.
title_cn: 联合精度神经网络：任务感知依赖性与预测性学习
summary_cn: 该论文提出了一种联合优化框架（PNN-Joint），可同时估计稀疏的精度矩阵和图神经网络权重。其任务感知的图推断能力和在小样本数据中的鲁棒性，在组合优化和风险管理的金融应用中具有潜在价值，尤其适用于识别市场隐藏依赖关系。

title: MiniCorp: The Last Mile of the AI Agent Firm
summary: The last mile toward enterprise AGI is a company that runs itself. Training and adapting such agents require longitudinal enterprise data, which remain scarce, costly to acquire, and often restricted by privacy constraints. Historical archives are also frequently incomplete and record only what actually happened. They cannot show the outcomes of alternative decisions. We introduce MiniCorp, an office simulator for studying how agents can collectively run a company while generating enterprise data at scale. Using an e-commerce company as a demonstration, MiniCorp connects two interacting worlds. The external world models customers, dynamic competitors, and market mechanisms. The internal world consists of agents that observe events, discuss their options, and make strategic decisions. These decisions have lasting effects on the market, and the resulting feedback informs the firm's later decisions. As the firm and market interact, MiniCorp continuously records the agents' communications and decisions. These records preserve the information available at the time and the business results that followed. Checkpointing allows the same situation to be replayed under different decisions, providing comparisons unavailable in static archives. We evaluate end-to-end fidelity against patterns reported in empirical studies of real markets. These evaluations provide agents with realistic market feedback and reduce the risk that they learn to exploit flaws in the simulator. Our experiments show agents coordinating across roles and adapting their decisions to market feedback. With explicit long-term strategic guidance, they also sustain advertising exploration despite weak early returns. MiniCorp thus provides an environment for studying AI-run companies and a scalable source of longitudinal and counterfactual enterprise data for agent training and evaluation.
core_methodology: MiniCorp introduces an office simulator where AI agents collectively run a company in a simulated e-commerce environment. The methodology involves modeling external market dynamics (customers, competitors, market mechanisms) and internal agent decision-making processes, with agents observing, discussing, and making strategic decisions that impact the market. The system includes checkpointing for counterfactual analysis and records all communications and decisions for longitudinal and counterfactual data generation.
data_sources: Simulated e-commerce company data, including customer interactions, market dynamics, and internal agent communications and decisions. The data is generated through interactions between agents and a simulated market environment, with the capability to replay scenarios under different decisions.
alpha_potential: The simulated environment can be used to explore and test trading strategies in a controlled setting before deploying them in real markets. The counterfactual analysis allows for evaluating the outcomes of different strategic decisions, which can be translated into predictive models for real-world trading. The longitudinal data can help in understanding long-term effects of strategies, and the agent coordination mechanisms may inspire new algorithmic trading approaches.
title_cn: MiniCorp：AI代理企业的最后一英里
summary_cn: MiniCorp是一个办公室模拟器，用于研究AI代理如何集体运营公司并大规模生成企业数据。通过模拟电子商务公司的内外部环境，系统记录代理的通信和决策，支持重放不同决策下的情景。该模拟环境可测试交易策略，并通过反事实分析评估不同决策的效果，为实际交易提供预测模型。

title: Learning to Simulate Individuals from Macro Social Signals
summary: Large language models are increasingly used to simulate how individuals respond to new situations, yet the behavioral reasoning behind these responses is either inherited from pretraining or learned from individual-level annotations, which offer limited behavioral diversity and little supervision of the reasoning itself. We propose to learn behavioral reasoning from prediction markets, whose price trajectories record how populations respond to real-world events at scale. We introduce macro2mind, which trains a language model with GRPO using market signals. A social behavioral decomposition makes behavioral reasoning an explicit step of forecasting: the model infers representative groups of market participants, predicts how each interprets the news and updates its beliefs, reasons about their interactions, and aggregates these responses into a price. A hindsight-regret curriculum with difficulty-aware sampling focuses training on transitions where hindsight-identified groups substantially improve the forecast while prioritizing examples that remain learnable for the current policy. The learned reasoning applies to user simulation without further training. On SWM-Bench, macro2mind achieves state-of-the-art directional accuracy and correlation on Polymarket. Trained on market data, it transfers zero-shot to four user-simulation benchmarks (Humanual, OvertonBench, PRISM, and CAD) and has competitive performance among zero-shot methods. Used as a data generator, macro2mind also raises a downstream simulator's accuracy on unseen users by 15.5 points, outperforming data generated by its backbone by 13.2 points.
core_methodology: The paper introduces macro2mind, which uses prediction market price trajectories to train a language model (with GRPO) to simulate individual behavioral reasoning. The model decomposes social behavior into explicit steps: inferring market participant groups, predicting belief updates, reasoning about interactions, and aggregating into price predictions. A curriculum learning approach focuses on critical transitions and learnable examples.
data_sources: Prediction markets (Polymarket specifically mentioned) which capture population-level responses to real-world events. Also tested on user-simulation benchmarks (Humanual, OvertonBench, PRISM, CAD).
alpha_potential: The methodology could uncover unique behavioral patterns in market participants that aren't captured by traditional models, potentially leading to novel sentiment indicators or early detection of regime changes. The transfer learning capability suggests it may identify universal behavioral triggers across different domains.
title_cn: 从宏观社会信号学习个体行为模拟
summary_cn: 该研究通过预测市场数据训练语言模型，显式建模市场参与群体的行为推理过程（包括信念更新和群体交互），并采用课程学习优化关键转折点的预测。在Polymarket上实现最先进的预测精度，且能零样本迁移至用户模拟任务。对量化交易的潜在价值在于：1）从市场行为中挖掘新型情绪因子 2）检测市场机制转换早期信号 3）通过行为分解识别群体博弈模式。

title: Finite-Sample Distribution Theory and Efficient Large-Scale Inference for Online Quantile Regression
summary: This paper studies online quantile regression for large-scale and streaming data using Stochastic SubGradient Descent (SSGD) with constant learning rates. Classical offline inference for quantile regression is computationally and memory intensive. Existing works of online inference for quantile regression provide only asymptotic guarantees and typically require sub-exponential tail conditions for distribution theory. To bridge these gaps, we introduce new techniques to prove a quenched central limit theorem (CLT) and finite-sample Gaussian approximation for SSGD under a finite-moment assumption. We further show that Ruppert-Polyak averaging with a constant learning rate has a non-vanishing bias and fails to satisfy CLT centering at the population target. Hence we propose suffix averaging to address this issue and establish its finite-sample Gaussian approximation. Based on these results, we provide an efficient online inference method for quantile regression that avoids covariance estimation. Numerical experiments show that our method achieves desirable empirical coverage rates and competitive performance compared to other inference methods. We also apply our approach to U.S. wage data to demonstrate its practical effectiveness.
core_methodology: Online quantile regression via Stochastic SubGradient Descent (SSGD) with constant learning rates and suffix averaging, avoiding computationally intensive offline methods and providing finite-sample guarantees.
data_sources: Demonstrated on U.S. wage data, but the methodology is applicable to high-frequency financial time series and streaming market data.
alpha_potential: Enables real-time quantile estimation for risk management (e.g., VaR), volatility modeling, and anomaly detection in financial data streams. Particularly valuable for momentum/mean-reversion strategies that rely on quantile-based regime detection.
title_cn: 在线分位数回归的有限样本分布理论及高效大规模推断方法
summary_cn: 本研究提出一种基于随机次梯度下降的在线分位数回归方法，针对金融高频数据流的实时处理优化计算效率与统计推断能力。无需估计协方差矩阵即可实现稳健的区间估计，适用于市场风险监测、波动率建模及分位数交易策略的动态调整。

title: FreSia: Frequency-Semantic Instantiation and Alignment for Multivariate Time Series Analysis
summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown strong potential in multivariate time series forecasting and anomaly detection. Existing studies predominantly inject temporal information into LLMs via direct numerical tokenization or heuristic textual descriptions. However, LLMs still face difficulty in perceiving the underlying structural patterns of numerical time series, particularly the seasonal and trend components obscured by discrete numerical tokens. To bridge this gap, we propose FreSia, a frequency-aware framework that establishes an effective alignment between the semantic space of LLMs and the frequency space of time series. Specifically, FGPrompt, a Frequency-Guided Prompt mechanism within FreSia, distills the frequency-domain structures of time series and projects them into prompts tailored to the semantic space of LLMs. Furthermore, we introduce a Global-driven Context Learning (GCL) component, which uses a global CLS-driven probe to generate global context to bridge the time-frequency domain gap and fuse the multi-modal information. Experiments on eight forecasting benchmarks show that FreSia achieves average improvements of 13.48% and 8.06% in MSE and MAE, respectively.
core_methodology: Frequency-Semantic Instantiation and Alignment for Multivariate Time Series Analysis via LLMs, focusing on frequency-aware framework (FreSia) with Frequency-Guided Prompt (FGPrompt) mechanism and Global-driven Context Learning (GCL) component.
data_sources: Multivariate time series data, likely applicable to financial market data including price, volume, and other relevant time series.
alpha_potential: Potential to uncover hidden seasonal and trend components obscured by discrete numerical tokens, providing more accurate forecasting and anomaly detection in financial time series, which can be leveraged for trading signals.
title_cn: FreSia: 多变量时间序列分析的频率-语义实例化与对齐
summary_cn: FreSia 是一种频率感知框架，通过LLMs的语义空间与时间序列的频率空间对齐，显著提升了时间序列预测和异常检测的准确性。其核心组件FGPrompt和GCL能够有效识别时间序列的潜在结构和趋势，为量化交易提供更精准的信号生成。

title: Voltic: Distinguishing Volatility from Stochasticity in Recurrent Memory
summary: Recurrent sequence models must decide how strongly to overwrite their memory at each token. Read as Bayesian filtering, this write is the gain of a Kalman update, set by uncertainty from two sources that pull it in opposite directions: volatility, how quickly the underlying associations change, and stochasticity, how noisy each observation of them is. First, we show that the update of gated delta-rule memories is the form this filter takes under isotropic uncertainty. Next, we introduce Voltic, a recurrent memory that keeps the covariance anisotropic and makes both noise variances input-dependent, so the write is vector-valued and carries uncertainty accumulated over the sequence. A dense covariance would have to be propagated token by token, ruling out the parallel training these models depend on. We therefore give two assumed-density approximations, diagonal and quasi-diagonal, both of which leave the memory update in delta-rule form and reuse its chunked kernels. On controlled recall tasks in which associations change and observations are corrupted, Voltic leads all baselines. On the task combining volatility and stochasticity, its margin over the strongest baseline is larger at both extrapolation sizes than at the training sizes. In 45M-parameter language models it leads an eight-task reasoning average and achieves higher retrieval accuracy beyond the training context length than gated baselines, at throughput close to those baselines. Deriving the write from an uncertainty recursion therefore makes memory more responsive to change.
core_methodology: Voltic introduces a recurrent neural memory architecture that dynamically distinguishes between volatility (rate of association changes) and stochasticity (observation noise) at each timestep. The model maintains anisotropic covariance matrices and implements input-dependent noise variances, enabling vector-valued memory updates that propagate uncertainty accumulation through sequences. Key innovations include: 1) Bayesian filtering approach to memory updates modeled as Kalman gain optimization, 2) Two efficient approximations (diagonal and quasi-diagonal) for practical implementation while maintaining parallel training capability, 3) Delta-rule form memory updates with chunked kernels.
data_sources: While not explicitly tested on financial data in the paper, the methodology is designed for sequential data processing and has been validated on controlled recall tasks (simulating changing associations and noisy observations) and language modeling tasks requiring long-range dependencies.
alpha_potential: This architecture shows promise for: 1) Time-series forecasting where signal-to-noise ratio varies (e.g., regime detection in volatile markets), 2) Event-driven trading where information reliability needs dynamic weighting, 3) Modeling market microstructure effects where observation quality varies with liquidity conditions. The demonstrated ability to outperform baselines on tasks combining volatility and stochasticity suggests potential for creating more robust trading signals in noisy environments.
title_cn: Voltic：在循环记忆中区分波动性与随机性
summary_cn: Voltic提出了一种创新的循环记忆架构，通过动态区分关联变化率（波动性）与观测噪声（随机性）来优化记忆更新。该方法采用各向异性协方差和输入相关的噪声建模，在序列任务中展现出优于基线的性能，尤其适合金融市场中信噪比动态变化的情景。其贝叶斯滤波框架和高效实现方式为处理高频交易数据中的不确定性和状态跃迁提供了新的技术路径。

title: Round-Trip KNN Clustering: multiscale hierarchical cluster detection on directed nearest-neighbour graphs
summary: We introduce Round-Trip KNN Clustering (RTKNNC), a graph-based method for finding cluster structure at several neighbourhood scales without requiring the number of clusters in advance. Unlike approaches that first make a $k$-nearest-neighbour (KNN) graph undirected, RTKNNC keeps both directions of the neighbour relation: which points a given point selects and which points select it. Incoming selections are treated as weighted votes that help decide which local connections remain visible during a recursive forward-and-reverse traversal. Repeating the procedure for increasing $K$ reveals how groups persist or merge as the neighbourhood scale grows; for the reference inverse-square model before structural refinement, clusters can merge but do not split. Because graph connectivity can occasionally join distinct groups through a sparse bridge or a small region of overlap, we add an optional label-free refinement. It first tests whether an already formed component is better described by two or three Gaussian subpopulations, and accepts a subdivision only when the proposed groups are large enough and consistent with the visible KNN graph. Across eight synthetic datasets and $K=2,\ldots,16$, independent C and Python implementations produced identical partitions in all 120 reference runs. Refinement increased adjusted Rand index from $0.7817$ to $0.9627$ on a variable-density benchmark and from $0.8083$ to $0.9853$ on a sparse-bridge benchmark. Comparisons with seven external clustering methods show competitive performance while preserving a label-free cluster-construction process.
core_methodology: Round-Trip KNN Clustering (RTKNNC) is a graph-based clustering method that utilizes both directions of nearest-neighbor relationships (incoming and outgoing) to detect hierarchical cluster structures across multiple scales without requiring predefined cluster counts. It includes an optional refinement step using Gaussian subpopulation testing to improve cluster separation.
data_sources: While the paper demonstrates performance on synthetic datasets, the methodology is theoretically applicable to market microstructure data, asset price time series, or other financial datasets requiring hierarchical clustering.
alpha_potential: Potential applications include detecting regime changes in market conditions, identifying groups of correlated assets for statistical arbitrage, or clustering order flow patterns in market microstructure analysis. The multiscale clustering could help identify hierarchical relationships in complex financial datasets.
title_cn: 往返K最近邻聚类：基于有向最近邻图的多尺度层次聚类检测
summary_cn: 本文提出的往返KNN聚类方法通过保留最近邻关系的双向信息，实现了无需预设聚类数的多尺度层次聚类。该方法可能应用于金融市场微观结构分析、资产相关性分组或市场状态识别，其层次聚类特性特别适合分析金融数据的复杂层级关系。

title: To Learn is to Wander: Learning Across Graphs and Tasks with Random Walks
summary: Graph foundation models aim to transfer across graphs, feature spaces, relational schemas, and prediction tasks, yet existing approaches typically generalize only within particular graph modalities or tasks. We propose Wander, a graph foundation model designed to operate across these settings within a single pretrained checkpoint. Following the prior-predictive perspective, we formulate graph learning as completion of a partially observed graph. We realize this task-general view through a common interface based on random walks, allowing the same model to operate across homogeneous and multi-relational graphs with varying features, labels, and relational schemas. Wander can increase its structural context at inference time without changing its learned parameters and, under suitable assumptions, universally approximates the corresponding Bayes-optimal predictor on bounded connected graphs. Empirically, a single pretrained checkpoint achieves state-of-the-art or highly competitive results across node classification, homogeneous link prediction, and knowledge-graph link prediction. Moreover, joint pretraining across graph modalities and tasks preserves performance in specialized settings while enabling positive transfer and the composition of separately learned capabilities at inference time.
core_methodology: The paper introduces Wander, a graph foundation model utilizing random walks to learn across different graph structures and tasks. It operates across homogeneous and multi-relational graphs with varying features, labels, and relational schemas, achieving state-of-the-art results in node classification and link prediction.
data_sources: The methodology is designed to work with any graph-structured data, which in finance could include transaction networks, social networks of traders, or knowledge graphs of financial entities.
alpha_potential: Potential applications in finance include detecting anomalies in transaction networks, predicting links in financial knowledge graphs (e.g., company relationships), and analyzing temporal patterns in market participant behavior. The model's ability to generalize across different graph structures could be valuable for multi-asset or cross-market analysis.
title_cn: 学习即漫游：通过随机游走在图和任务间进行学习
summary_cn: 该研究提出的Wander模型通过随机游走技术实现跨图表和任务的通用学习，在金融领域可用于交易网络分析、实体关系预测等多场景。虽然目前侧重于理论框架，但其处理异构金融图谱的能力对跨资产相关性分析和异常交易检测具有潜在价值。

title: Empirical Variational Autoencoder
summary: We present Empirical Variational Autoencoder, a general generative framework for continuous-valued (i.e., non-vector-quantized) sequences. EVA is based on the evidence lower bound of the Variational Autoencoder (VAE) but learns autoregressive latent priors empirically from training data, which can be implemented only by an additional single linear layer on top of VAEs. By replacing the conventional standard-Gaussian constraint with the self-predicted priors, EVA significantly alleviates the latent distribution gap between prior and posterior which is typically observed in conventional VAEs, and leads to high-fidelity ancestral sampling for sequential data generation. Extensive experiments on image and sound synthesis demonstrate that EVA achieves competitive generation quality with autoregressive diffusion baselines despite its much faster inference time.
core_methodology: Empirical Variational Autoencoder (EVA) with autoregressive latent priors for sequential data generation
data_sources: Generic continuous-valued sequential data (tested on images and sound in paper)
alpha_potential: Potential for generating synthetic financial time series data or enhancing sequential pattern recognition in market data, though not directly demonstrated in paper
title_cn: 经验变分自编码器
summary_cn: 该论文提出的经验变分自编码器(EVA)通过自回归潜在先验显著改善了传统VAE的潜在分布差距。在量化交易中，该方法或可用于生成合成金融时序数据，或增强市场序列模式的识别能力，但需进一步验证其在金融数据上的表现。

title: WaveGSSM: Graph Wave State Space Models for Propagating Spatio-Temporal Patterns
summary: Spatio-temporal graph models typically encode each snapshot with a GNN and then connect the resulting representations through a temporal module. This space-then-time design is effective, yet it does not explicitly represent how a pattern moves across the graph. We show empirically that, for a propagating process, the same present field can lead to different futures when its recent rate of change differs, motivating an explicit representation of motion in the predictive state. We introduce WaveGSSM, a second-order graph state-space model that maintains two coupled latent states at each node, one for the current pattern and one for its temporal rate of change. A graph-wave transition updates the motion state through graph interactions and uses it to advance the pattern state, coupling spatial propagation and temporal evolution within a single rollout. We evaluate WaveGSSM on four temporal-graph benchmarks and global weather forecasting. It consistently achieves the best mean performance across the temporal-graph benchmarks and reduces the geopotential RMSE by 20.2% on average for 1- to 5-day weather forecasts relative to a backbone-matched snapshot model, while better preserving large-scale atmospheric patterns.
core_methodology: WaveGSSM introduces a second-order graph state-space model that maintains two coupled latent states at each node—one for the current pattern and one for its temporal rate of change. This approach explicitly models the propagation of spatio-temporal patterns across a graph, combining spatial interaction and temporal evolution in a single rollout.
data_sources: The paper evaluates performance using temporal-graph benchmarks and global weather forecasting data, which implies potential applicability to financial time-series data (e.g., asset price movements or order book dynamics).
alpha_potential: The model’s explicit representation of motion and propagation in spatio-temporal patterns could be valuable for detecting and forecasting momentum or mean-reversion patterns in multi-asset markets. The architecture’s ability to better preserve large-scale patterns suggests potential for macro-factor timing or cross-asset correlation modeling.
title_cn: WaveGSSM：用于时空模式传播的图波状态空间模型
summary_cn: WaveGSSM提出了一种新的二阶图状态空间模型，通过显式建模节点间时空模式的传播动态，为金融时间序列（如多资产动量传导或订单簿动态）提供了创新的预测框架。该模型在保留宏观模式方面的优势尤其适用于跨资产相关性建模或宏观因子择时策略开发。

title: Quantifying the Stability of Multi-Step Reasoning via Error Amplification
summary: We consider the stability of multi-step reasoning processes, which have extensive applications in language models, including chain-of-thought and algorithmic reasoning. While longer sequences of reasoning can improve a model's generation capability at test time, the errors due to intermediate reasoning steps can accumulate in autoregressive generation, and thus grow substantially at the end. In this paper, we ask: What are the key factors determining the stability of multi-step reasoning? First, we show an inference error bound governed by the product of spectral norms of the Jacobians taken through the input space across generation steps. This product can be viewed as an error amplification factor, which could scale exponentially with the number of reasoning steps, serving as a quantitative measure of reasoning stability. Second, we analyze this measure in transformer models trained to predict simple tasks like linear and quadratic functions. We theoretically prove that the transformer model converges to a solution where the stability measure decays, thus yielding nearly zero inference loss over (arbitrarily) long steps. Finally, the stability analysis leads to several algorithmic implications for controlling the stability, through (i) chain-of-thought length compression that reduces the sensitivity of each step, and (ii) quantization-aware training that regularizes the input Jacobian norms. We validate the proposed algorithms by fine-tuning language models on graph-algorithmic reasoning tasks and symbolic state-tracking tasks. Across seven evaluations, our algorithms improve over baseline comparisons by 3.5% on average, and by 8.2% for longer-length inputs. Ablation analysis validates that the stability measure is drastically reduced by 3-8$\times$, confirming the regularization effect on the spectral norms of the (input space) Jacobians.
core_methodology: Analysis of error amplification in multi-step reasoning processes in transformer models, including theoretical proofs and algorithmic implications for controlling stability.
data_sources: Transformer models trained on simple tasks like linear and quadratic functions, and fine-tuned on graph-algorithmic reasoning and symbolic state-tracking tasks.
alpha_potential: Potential to improve the stability and accuracy of multi-step reasoning in trading strategies, particularly in algorithmic decision-making and predictive modeling.
title_cn: 通过误差放大量化多步推理的稳定性
summary_cn: 本文研究了多步推理过程中的误差放大问题，提出了通过Jacobian矩阵的谱范数乘积来量化推理稳定性，并通过链式思维长度压缩和量化感知训练来控制稳定性。在金融交易中，该方法可提升多步预测模型的准确性和鲁棒性，适用于算法交易和量化策略优化。

title: Learning Pareto Stationary Fronts via Single-Pass Backpropagation
summary: We propose MOSEL (Multi-Objective Stackelberg Efficient Learning), a framework for a posteriori multi-objective optimization (MOO) in deep neural networks that recovers a full front of Pareto stationary solutions at the computational cost of standard single-objective training. MOSEL reformulates the problem as a bilevel optimization problem that leverages network modularity to decouple representation learning from objective-preference alignment. Casting the bilevel optimization problem as a Stackelberg game enables solving the original a posteriori MOO problem in a single forward-backward pass. As a result, MOSEL matches the time and memory efficiency of standard single-objective training while enabling scalable Pareto stationary front learning. Empirically, MOSEL uncovers diverse and optimal Pareto frontiers in strongly conflicting settings (e.g., fairness-accuracy). Remarkably, even in weakly conflicting regimes such as multi-task learning, it consistently converges to solutions closer to the utopia point, outperforming both standard single-objective training and specialized multi-task learning methods. These results highlight the broader potential of a posteriori MOO learning as a pathway to efficiently learn more diverse and robust representations, ultimately improving generalization.
core_methodology: The paper proposes MOSEL (Multi-Objective Stackelberg Efficient Learning), a bilevel optimization framework that uses Stackelberg game theory to solve multi-objective optimization problems in neural networks. It efficiently learns Pareto stationary fronts with computational cost comparable to single-objective training.
data_sources: Not explicitly mentioned in the abstract, but the methodology is general and could potentially be applied to financial data such as price series, factor exposures, or portfolio weights.
alpha_potential: This method could be valuable in portfolio optimization problems where multiple objectives (e.g., risk minimization, return maximization, transaction cost control) need to be balanced simultaneously. The efficient Pareto optimization could help find better trade-offs than traditional approaches.
title_cn: 通过单次反向传播学习帕累托稳态前沿
summary_cn: 该论文提出的MOSEL框架通过使用Stackelberg博弈理论实现高效的帕累托前沿优化，可应用于量化投资的组合优化问题，同时考虑收益、风险和控制成本等多个目标，在计算效率上与单目标训练相当。

title: Capability-Driven Self-Evolution of Agent Memory
summary: Memory self-evolution uses task feedback to iteratively improve executable memory programs that store and retrieve information from past interactions. Existing approaches typically adopt holistic evolution, deriving revision directions from mixed feedback and judging progress by overall performance. This can obscure optimization directions and hide capability-specific gains offset by regressions elsewhere, leaving promising directions underexplored. We introduce capability-driven evolution, which extends search guidance from overall performance to individual capability dimensions, preserving promising revisions and expanding exploration beyond the boundaries of holistic evolution. We propose PrisMem, which uses dependency-aware capability selection to prioritize targets with potential cross-capability benefits and history-guided diagnosis to refine capability specialists. Trace-guided integration compares evaluated programs on paired differential cases, using their behavioral differences to consolidate complementary gains into a unified memory program. Experiments show that PrisMem outperforms the strongest baselines by 10.54 and 7.83 percentage points on BEAM-1M and LongMemEval-M, respectively, demonstrating its effectiveness on million-token histories.
core_methodology: Capability-driven self-evolution of agent memory that improves memory programs through task feedback, utilizing dependency-aware capability selection and history-guided diagnosis to refine memory specialists.
data_sources: Not explicitly mentioned, but applicable to any sequential or interaction-based data, which could include financial time series or market interaction data.
alpha_potential: Potential to enhance trading agents' ability to store and retrieve relevant information from past market interactions, improving decision-making in dynamic environments.
title_cn: 基于能力驱动的智能体记忆自进化
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种能力驱动的智能体记忆自进化方法，通过任务反馈改进记忆程序，适用于金融交易中的动态决策环境。其依赖感知能力选择和历史指导诊断可优化记忆专家，提升交易系统对历史信息的处理能力。

title: Do Small Language Models Learn to Negotiate? A Controlled Scaling Study of RL-Trained Sellers
summary: LLM agents are starting to own the full customer experience. Soon, LLMs may be selling and buying on behalf of companies and customers respectively. Small models are more cost-efficient at scale, but can reinforcement learning train them into competent sellers? We train four Gemma 4 checkpoints (2.3B to 31B effective parameters) with GRPO on a programmatic utility reward for bilateral multi-issue bargaining, and evaluate every arm on the same 1,152 negotiations against two frontier buyers it never saw in training. With the same learning rate ($10^{-6}$) for every size, the gain of the RL model over its base rises from $+0.001$ at 2.3B to $+0.078$ at 31B. Each size was trained once and the two smallest checkpoints use a different architecture, so we fit no scaling law. Tripling the learning rate, with the same or fewer training steps, improves on the shared rate at every size by $+0.032$ (2.3B) to $+0.081$ (4.5B). In exploratory comparisons with two frontier models run as sellers, the 12B seller trained at the tripled rate scores above both, though its untrained base already scores as high as they do. The 4.5B seller at that rate shows no detectable difference from either and fits on one 48 GB GPU. A further 2.3B arm at ten times the shared rate raises pooled score, but its gain concentrates on the evaluation buyer that shares a model family with the training pool. These results suggest tuning the learning rate before concluding that a small model cannot learn to negotiate, and testing against buyers from more than one model family.
core_methodology: Reinforcement learning applied to language models for negotiation tasks, with scaling studies across model sizes (2.3B to 31B parameters) and learning rate optimization
data_sources: Synthetic negotiation environment with bilateral multi-issue bargaining scenarios
alpha_potential: Demonstrates potential for AI-driven negotiation agents in financial contexts (e.g., OTC trading, counterparty negotiations), though requires adaptation from general negotiation to financial use cases. Shows that smaller models can be competitive with proper RL tuning
title_cn: 小型语言模型能否学会谈判？一项关于强化学习训练卖家的控制性规模研究
summary_cn: 本研究通过强化学习训练不同规模的Gemma模型（2.3B至31B参数）进行双边多议题谈判，发现合适的学习率调整可使较小的12B模型性能超越前沿模型。研究表明小模型在金融领域谈判场景（如场外交易谈判）中存在应用潜力，但需注意训练对手的多样性。

title: Anlu: Enabling In-Context Time Series Anomaly Detection in Foundation Models via Counterfactual Supervision
summary: Whether a time-series pattern is anomalous often depends on the operating regime of the monitored process. A missing event can signal a fault in one regime and be routine in another, and the query alone may not reveal which regime applies. We study in-context learning (ICL) for time series anomaly detection (TSAD) through reference-conditioned detection, where a reference record provides evidence about expected behavior and model parameters remain fixed at inference. Supplying the reference is not enough: when training anomalies are recognizable from the query alone, the detector can fit its targets while ignoring the reference. We therefore introduce counterfactual supervision, which pairs one query with two references that support different normal rules and labels the query under each. At positions where the two labels disagree, no detector that ignores the reference can fit both targets. Anlu learns from this supervision by adding a reference memory and zero-initialized gated adapters to a frozen time-series foundation model (TSFM) pretrained for anomaly detection. On the 350 TSB-AD-U evaluation sequences, Anlu raises the mean VUS-PR of the frozen TSFM from 0.542 to 0.607. Replacing the reference with zeros lowers Anlu's score to 0.499.
core_methodology: The paper introduces Anlu, a method for in-context time series anomaly detection (TSAD) using counterfactual supervision. It leverages reference-conditioned detection where a reference record provides context for expected behavior, and employs zero-initialized gated adapters on a frozen time-series foundation model (TSFM) pretrained for anomaly detection.
data_sources: The paper evaluates the method on 350 TSB-AD-U time series sequences, which are synthetic or real-world time-series datasets for anomaly detection.
alpha_potential: The methodology could be adapted for detecting anomalous patterns in financial time series (e.g., price, volume, or order flow data), potentially identifying regime changes or rare events that precede market movements.
title_cn: Anlu：通过反事实监督在基础模型中实现上下文时间序列异常检测
summary_cn: Anlu通过上下文学习进行时间序列异常检测，使用参考记录提供正常行为的证据。该方法结合反事实监督和冻结的时间序列基础模型，可应用于金融市场中识别价格或交易量数据的异常模式，潜在用于检测市场状态变化或预测罕见事件。在350个评估序列上表现出显著性能提升。

title: TIGER: Time-Series Classification with In-Context-Learning Gated Ensemble of Representations
summary: A representation family is a distinct way of extracting features from time series. Ensemble algorithms that combine several representation families remain the most accurate approach to time series classification. Current state-of-the-art ensembles, most notably HIVE-COTE~2.0, pair a bespoke classification algorithm with each representation family and combine their predictions using a fixed, non-adaptive rule. We present TIGER (Time-series classification with In-context-learning Gated Ensemble of Representations), which instead applies the same small portfolio of three general-purpose classifiers (Ridge, Extra Trees, and Naive Bayes) to four representations from four distinct families, stacking the resulting twelve base learners' predictions into a meta-feature matrix. The final prediction is produced by an adaptive meta-classification rule that chooses, independently for each data set, between a weighted hard majority vote and TabICLv2, a pretrained tabular foundation model used in-context as a meta-classifier, based on the mean number of training samples available per class. On a 142-data-set benchmark drawn from the UCR time series classification archive, TIGER obtains the best mean accuracy, balanced accuracy, and F1-score among six compared algorithms, including HIVE-COTE~2.0, and significantly outperforms each of the other five individually. TIGER's adaptive rule also meaningfully outperforms either of its two constituent meta-classification methods used alone, and its single hyperparameter, tuned using only a twenty-data-set development subset, is shown to generalize to the full evaluation benchmark. We further characterize TIGER's design through an extensive set of ablation experiments and report the design alternatives that we investigated and ultimately discarded.
core_methodology: TIGER combines four distinct time series representation families with three general-purpose classifiers (Ridge, Extra Trees, Naive Bayes) into an ensemble. It uses an adaptive meta-classification rule that chooses between weighted hard majority vote and a pretrained tabular foundation model (TabICLv2) based on class sample size.
data_sources: UCR time series classification archive (142 dataset benchmark), not financial market data but general time series datasets
alpha_potential: Potential application in financial time series classification/prediction tasks (e.g., regime detection, pattern recognition) through adaptation of its ensemble methodology, though not directly tested on market data. The adaptive meta-classification approach could be valuable for handling non-stationary market conditions.
title_cn: TIGER：基于上下文学习门控表征集成的时间序列分类方法
summary_cn: TIGER创新性地将四种时间序列表征方法与三种通用分类器结合，通过自适应元分类规则实现最优预测。其方法论对金融时间序列模式识别（如市场状态分类、价格形态检测）有潜在应用价值，尤其适应不同样本规模的数据特性，有助于开发稳健的交易信号生成系统。

title: Pay to Learn, Share to Earn: Incentivized Federated Multi-Player Bandits
summary: Federated multi-player multi-armed bandit problems model collaborative sequential decision-making where multiple players interact with a common bandit environment and share information through a central server to accelerate learning. Existing federated bandit frameworks typically assume that all players willingly share their local observations with the server. However, this assumption is often unrealistic in practical settings where players are self-interested and may not participate in collaboration without explicit incentives. To address this challenge, we propose an incentive-aware federated bandit framework in which players receive rewards for sharing information with the server and incur costs when buying information from the server. We develop a UCB-based algorithm, termed Buying-UCB, that balances individual exploration and collaborative learning by incorporating both sharing incentives and information acquisition costs into the learning process. We theoretically analyze the proposed algorithm and derive upper bounds on the group regret and buying cost. Our analysis further characterizes the trade-off between fully collaborative federated learning and completely independent learning. Extensive numerical experiments validate the theoretical findings and demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework under different collaboration and pricing regimes.
core_methodology: Incentivized federated multi-player multi-armed bandit algorithm (Buying-UCB) that balances exploration-exploitation trade-offs with explicit reward mechanisms for information sharing and costs for information acquisition.
data_sources: Generic sequential decision-making environment (could be adapted to market data streams or alternative data sources in trading contexts).
alpha_potential: Potential to model collaboration among proprietary trading teams or hedge funds sharing signals while maintaining incentive compatibility. May improve discovery of profitable strategies through controlled information exchange.
title_cn: 付费学习，分享获利：激励式联邦多玩家老虎机
summary_cn: 本论文提出的激励式联邦多玩家老虎机框架，通过中央服务器协调自利玩家之间的信息共享与购买机制，可潜在应用于量化交易领域。其核心算法Buying-UCB在平衡个体探索与协作学习方面的创新，为不同量化团队间安全分享交易信号提供了理论支持，可能提升策略开发效率。

title: Adaptive Expert Guidance for Efficient On-Policy Reinforcement Learning
summary: With massively parallel simulation, on-policy Reinforcement Learning methods such as PPO have become standard in many domains. However, learning from scratch is sample-inefficient and fails to exploit the potential existence of a suboptimal expert, such as a heuristic, a model-based controller, or a policy trained on a related task. Such an expert is often available and can guide early training, but its sub-optimality limits final performance. The challenge then becomes balancing expert guidance against learning from rewards. Existing methods set the expert's influence through a blending weight, a schedule, or an evaluation-driven curriculum. Alternatively, they adapt it with additional learned components such as critics over expert actions or auxiliary agents. However, none optimizes it using the same on-policy objective as the policy itself. We propose a method in which the learner and the expert alternate control within each training episode, and the expert's share of control is a single learnable parameter optimized jointly with the policy. The learner benefits from the expert early in training, but its share of control declines as the learner becomes more competent, until eventually vanishing completely. This leaves the learner acting alone and better than the suboptimal expert. We evaluate our method on 34 tasks across two benchmarks, spanning discrete and continuous action spaces, using both learned and model-based experts. Our method improves sample efficiency over guided and unguided baselines while requiring minimal hyperparameter variation. The expert's share decays to zero as the learner improves, vanishing when the expert is no longer useful.
core_methodology: The paper proposes a method for optimizing the balance between expert guidance and on-policy learning in reinforcement learning. The learner and expert alternate control within each training episode, with the expert's share of control being a learnable parameter optimized jointly with the policy. This allows the learner to benefit from the expert early in training, while gradually reducing reliance as the learner improves.
data_sources: The paper evaluates the method on 34 tasks across two benchmarks, spanning discrete and continuous action spaces, using both learned and model-based experts. While not directly financial, the methodology could be applied to trading if adapted.
alpha_potential: The adaptive expert guidance approach could potentially improve the sample efficiency of training trading policies by leveraging existing suboptimal strategies (heuristics, model-based controllers, or policies from related tasks) to bootstrap learning, while eventually outperforming them.
title_cn: 高效在策略强化学习的自适应专家指导方法
summary_cn: 该论文提出了一种在强化学习中自适应平衡专家指导与策略学习的方法。通过将专家控制比例作为可学习参数联合优化，使学习器能早期受益于专家知识，后期能超越次优专家。该方法可应用于交易策略训练，提高样本效率，具有潜在改进现有量化策略开发的实用价值。

title: Spectral Geometry of Attention: From Information Routing to Uncertainty
summary: In this work, we study transformer attention through the lens of spectral geometry and operator theory. We view each attention head as a functional map between Hilbert spaces of functions on the token sequence and derive a Token Difference Operator, whose spectral structure controls how token-space information is routed to the output. We show that standard Euclidean spectra are structurally biased by sinks, conflating mass concentration with genuine routing capacity. By recasting token space in the intrinsic probability geometry induced by attention, the token difference spectrum disentangles sink effects from routing capacity and provides a spectral description of the dimensionality of the head output. This yields a unified framework for analyzing attention maps, explaining sinks, routing collapse, and output dimensionality within a single operator-theoretic framework. In practice, by grounding attention heuristics in spectral geometry, we develop a novel attention-based uncertainty estimator that complements probability-based scores, with the largest gains on long-context inputs.
core_methodology: The paper introduces a spectral geometry approach to analyze transformer attention mechanisms, focusing on token-space information routing and developing a novel attention-based uncertainty estimator.
data_sources: Not explicitly mentioned, but typically involves token sequences which could be adapted for financial time series data.
alpha_potential: Potential to improve transformer-based trading models by better understanding and utilizing attention mechanisms for information routing and uncertainty estimation, particularly in long-context inputs.
title_cn: 注意力的谱几何：从信息路由到不确定性
summary_cn: 本研究通过谱几何和算子理论分析变压器注意力机制，提出了一种新的注意力不确定性估计方法，可能增强基于注意力的金融时间序列模型在长上下文输入中的表现。

title: Fast Last-Iterate Convergence in Zero-Sum Markov Games with Bandit Feedback
summary: We study last-iterate convergence in unknown two-player zero-sum discounted Markov games with bandit feedback. The players learn independently along a single trajectory without observing each other's actions. We develop Adaptive Regularized TD Learning (ARTD), which achieves a $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(t^{-1/4})$ duality gap bound for the current policies under a uniform hitting time assumption, with high probability simultaneously over all rounds and starting states. This improves the $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(t^{-1/(9+ν)})$ rate of Cai et al. (2023), for any fixed $ν>0$, under the same feedback model and hitting time assumption. Our algorithm requires no knowledge of the hitting time bound, the time horizon, or the confidence level. To stabilize policy learning as value estimates change, we separate fast temporal difference averaging from bounded value updates. We adapt log-barrier regularization to the progress of value estimation, controlling both policy and value errors throughout learning. Together, these mechanisms enable fast convergence of the policies actually played, even when the players learn independently from bandit feedback.
core_methodology: Adaptive Regularized TD Learning (ARTD) for last-iterate convergence in zero-sum Markov games with bandit feedback, focusing on temporal difference averaging and regularized policy updates
data_sources: Generic Markov game framework (could be mapped to market maker/taker interactions or other trading scenarios with opponents)
alpha_potential: Potential applications in adversarial trading environments (e.g., market making vs. arbitrageurs) or multi-agent trading systems where opponents' actions are not observable
title_cn: 具有Bandit反馈的零和马尔可夫博弈中的快速最后迭代收敛
summary_cn: 本研究提出了ARTD算法，在双人零和马尔可夫博弈背景下实现了快速的策略收敛，适用于对手行为不可观测的对抗性交易环境（如做市商与套利者间的博弈）。该算法通过自适应正则化TD学习和策略/价值误差控制，为量化交易中的多智能体系统优化提供了理论框架。

title: The Optimization Landscape of Learning Compacted Context Models
summary: Many works approach continual learning through the lens of infinite context windows. As an agent puts more observation into context (concretely the KV cache), compacting said context is akin to direct memory manipulation, without affecting the base model's weights. Many works pose KV compaction as an optimization problem: learn a smaller set of KV vectors that matches the behavior of the full KV cache. While this preserves base model behavior, optimizing through a frozen base model results in a highly nontrivial optimization problem with a brittle and flat loss landscape. In this paper, we characterize what makes these optimization problems difficult and demonstrate that a heavily simplified Perceiver-based architecture not only matches performance of a full Perceiver transformer in continuous context compaction, but outperforms baselines on compaction utility. Results are presented on MCQ tasks across Finance, Legal, Gutenberg, and Code.
core_methodology: Focuses on KV cache compaction through optimization and simplification of Perceiver-based architectures, aiming to maintain performance while reducing computational overhead.
data_sources: MCQ tasks across Finance, Legal, Gutenberg, and Code indicating multi-domain applicability including financial datasets.
alpha_potential: Potential for real-time processing of large financial contexts (like order book data or news feeds) with reduced memory footprint, aiding in latency-sensitive trading or sentiment analysis.
title_cn: 学习压缩上下文模型的优化格局
summary_cn: 本文通过优化KV缓存压缩方法，提出简化版Perceiver架构，在保持性能的同时降低内存使用。实验证明其在金融等多领域MCQ任务中优于基线，适合需要高效处理海量市场数据（如新闻流或订单簿）的低延迟交易场景。

title: Usefulness of Quantile-Aware Diffusion Modeling for Highly Imbalanced Tabular Data
summary: Classification problem in the context of highly imbalanced data is a major challenge in many real-world applications (e.g., FinTech, healthcare, etc.). In these cases, the vast majority of instances belong to a single class and a small fraction represent the minority class (often the most critical class). Recently, diffusion models have emerged as powerful approaches to reduce the degree of ``imbalanced-ness'' in the dataset; they work by generating synthetic data by capturing complex data distributions using iterative transformations. However, standard diffusion models are not inherently suited to highly skewed or heavy-tailed data, due to inbuilt quadratic error loss, which lacks the structural sensitivity to capture rare, extreme values, and minority-class nuances. We propose a novel approach, namely, Quantile-TabDDPM, based on a quantile-regularized denoising objective that combines the standard quadratic error loss with a quantile loss term to explicitly capture rare events while preserving the theoretical grounding of the original denoising objective. We extensively evaluated our approach on a real-world credit card transaction dataset characterized by extreme class imbalance. The results demonstrate that the integration of diffusion-based synthetic data generation with a quantile-regularized denoising objective provides a robust and effective framework for fraud detection in highly imbalanced datasets.
core_methodology: Quantile-regularized denoising diffusion model (Quantile-TabDDPM) combining quadratic error loss with quantile loss to handle extreme class imbalance in tabular data
data_sources: Credit card transaction datasets (financial fraud detection context), potentially applicable to other imbalanced financial datasets like corporate defaults or extreme market events
alpha_potential: Improved rare event detection capability could enhance fraud detection systems or predictive models for extreme market events, though direct trading strategy development would require additional work
title_cn: 分位数感知扩散模型在高不平衡表格数据中的应用价值
summary_cn: 该论文提出的Quantile-TabDDPM方法通过结合标准二次误差损失和分位数损失项，改进了传统扩散模型对极端不平衡金融数据的处理能力（如欺诈交易检测）。虽然直接应用于量化交易策略需进一步研发，但其技术路线对构建极端市场事件预警系统具有潜在价值。

title: Bellman-Centric Learning: Near-Optimal Regret for Linear Bandits with Memory
summary: We study linear bandits with memory, where past actions induce endogenous nonstationarity through an arbitrary known, bounded matrix-valued memory map. To trade off exploration and exploitation while accounting for the memory dynamics, we develop RSM-LinUCB, a Bellman-centric algorithm that learns as in linear bandits and plans as in reinforcement learning. This design admits a novel regret decomposition which separates the memory-induced error from the cumulative reward estimation error along the learner's trajectory. We prove a high-probability regret bound of $\widetilde O\big(dRS(M+1)+σd\sqrt T\big)$, where $T$ is the learning horizon, $d$ is the parameter dimension, $M$ is the memory length, $R$ and $S$ bound the memory-map operator norm and reward-parameter norm, respectively, and $σ$ is the sub-Gaussian noise scale. Our results reveal that the multiplicative memory-horizon coupling in prior bounds is not intrinsic: memory only contributes an additive cost, up to logarithmic factors. We also prove a matching minimax lower bound, establishing near-optimality. We further extend the algorithm to generalized linear rewards, preserving this separation with near-optimal memory and leading statistical dependence. Our algorithms outperform the baselines in numerical experiments on synthetic instances and semi-synthetic KV- and semantic-cache tasks.
core_methodology: The paper introduces RSM-LinUCB, a Bellman-centric algorithm combining techniques from linear bandits and reinforcement learning to handle memory dynamics in sequential decision-making. It features a novel regret decomposition separating memory effects from reward estimation errors.
data_sources: Theoretical framework with numerical validation on synthetic instances and semi-synthetic KV-/semantic-cache tasks (not financial data). Potentially applicable to any sequential decision problem with memory effects.
alpha_potential: Methodology could be adapted for: 1) Momentum strategies with memory effects, 2) Optimal order execution with delayed market impact, 3) Reinforcement learning for trading systems with historical dependencies. The additive (vs multiplicative) memory cost is particularly valuable for longer-horizon trading problems.
title_cn: 贝尔曼中心学习：具有记忆的线性赌博机近乎最优的遗憾界
summary_cn: 该研究提出的RSM-LinUCB算法通过贝尔曼方程融合线性赌博机与强化学习，解决记忆效应导致的非平稳性问题。在量化交易中，适用于需长期记忆建模的场景（如动量策略优化、订单流预测等），其加性（非乘性）记忆成本特性对高频交易尤其有价值。

title: The Premise Is the Problem: Exchangeability Failure in Self-Monitored Test-Time Adaptation
summary: Modern forecasting models are often updated after deployment so they can respond to changing data. These updates can also make predictions worse, so practical systems need a reliable monitor that can detect harmful changes and trigger protection. A natural design is to monitor the same prediction errors that guide the updates. This paper asks whether the statistical guarantee behind such a monitor remains valid when monitoring and adaptation use the same feedback. We study this question in multi-step time-series forecasting. We show that overlapping targets and dependence in forecast errors can break a key assumption required by the guarantee. The monitor may then raise alarms even when no harmful change has occurred, and its response can further damage prediction quality. We also find that adaptation can hide sustained changes from its own monitor, while the original frozen model retains a clearer signal. These results expose a basic failure mode in self-monitored adaptation. They show why reliable deployment requires checking the monitor's assumptions, comparing adaptation with the frozen model under realistic feedback, and limiting the effect of every protective response.
core_methodology: The paper examines the statistical guarantees of self-monitored adaptation in time-series forecasting models, highlighting issues with exchangeability when the same feedback is used for both monitoring and adaptation.
data_sources: Not explicitly mentioned, but presumably involves multi-step time-series forecasting data, which could include financial time-series data.
alpha_potential: The research could help in designing more robust adaptive trading models by addressing the pitfalls of self-monitored adaptation, potentially reducing false alarms and improving prediction quality.
title_cn: 前提即问题：自监督测试时适应中的可交换性失效
summary_cn: 本研究探讨了在时间序列预测中，自监督适应模型的统计保证问题，揭示了使用相同反馈进行监控和适应时可能出现的关键假设失效。这对设计更稳健的自适应交易模型具有潜在价值，可减少误报并提升预测质量。

title: Measuring Trade Direction in a Prediction Market: Settlement Ground Truth and Trading-Cost Measurement on Polymarket
summary: Trade-sign errors can change measured trading costs even when classification accuracy is high. We validate the side of Polymarket's public trade prints against the taker leg of each print's on-chain settlement. On twelve selected days between April and August 2026, spanning both exchange generations, 92.1% to 100.0% of prints match a settled taker leg, with exact side and token agreement on all 24.5 million matched pairs. Mint-and-merge settlement makes that taker leg essential: pooling maker and taker legs changes the measured buy share. Signing the full cached tape before settlement selection yields 16.6 million prints signed by every rule; equal-day balanced accuracy is 0.942 for Lee-Ready, 0.768 for the tick test and 0.670 for retrospective bulk volume classification. On 16.4 million identical eligible fills, Lee-Ready raises effective spread by 0.429 cents per share under equal-fill weights; its realised-spread difference is -0.209 cents. Under share-volume weights, taker five-minute midpoint impact is 0.689 cents, while tick and bulk classifications give -0.374 and -0.119 cents. That aggregate sign reversal disappears when tied print rows are excluded. Distortion depends on error-weighted signed outcomes, sample selection and weighting. Receipt-time ordering and unobserved future-quote age limit these delivered-quote accounting quantities; they do not identify causal impact or private information. Supporting venue and collector analyses provide descriptive diagnostics.
core_methodology: Validation of trade directions by comparing public trade prints against on-chain settlement data, with analysis of trading-cost measurement methodologies including Lee-Ready, tick test, and retrospective bulk volume classification.
data_sources: On-chain settlement data from Polymarket and public trade prints spanning twelve selected days between April and August 2026.
alpha_potential: The paper provides insights into trade-sign errors and their impact on trading cost measurement, which could help improve execution strategies and minimize costs in prediction markets.
title_cn: 预测市场中交易方向的测量：Polymarket上的结算真实性与交易成本测量
summary_cn: 该研究通过比较Polymarket公共交易单与链上结算数据，验证了交易方向准确性对交易成本测量的影响。92.1%到100%的交易单与结算数据一致。研究还分析了不同分类方法（Lee-Ready、tick test等）对有效价差的影响，为优化执行策略提供了重要参考。

title: Moment-Accurate Gaussian Mixtures for Constant-Step Stochastic Approximation
summary: Local Gaussian models of constant-step learning predict output variability and expected losses, but weak convergence alone does not justify these moment predictions.
